name: fig-11
title: fig-11: Evolution
question: Does the paper's §Evolution figure (Fig 11) hold as a runnable place-graph rewrite -- a top-level population of identically-schema'd cells, each exposing a scalar trait, evolving over generations toward a selection optimum set by the environmental niche, so that (Fig 11b) the trait distribution shifts toward the optimum via binary fission + heritable mutation + selection, while division itself (Fig 11a) is a discrete event that REPLACES a parent cell with two daughters?
biological_summary:
This is the runnable realization of the paper's §Evolution pattern (Fig 11), built on one process, `PopulationEvolution`, that reads and rewrites two `tree[node]` stores: a `population` of `cell` nodes that all share one schema -- each a heritable scalar `trait` plus a derived `division_rate` -- and an `environment` whose single `niche` node carries a `selection_optimum` that DRIFTS over the run. Each generation the process (1) shifts the optimum forward (a moving target), (2) re-scores every cell's division rate by a Gaussian fitness kernel on how close its trait sits to the current optimum, (3) performs BINARY FISSION -- a cell divides with probability `div_rate·fitness`, and on division the PARENT is deleted and REPLACED by two daughters, each inheriting the parent's trait ± Gaussian mutation, and (4) applies death by selection: once the population overflows carrying capacity, the least-fit cells (furthest from the optimum) die. This is the paper's §Evolution claim in action: evolution changes not the state of a single composition but the SPACE of compositions across generations -- new cell nodes are added and old ones removed at runtime, so the place graph itself is edited, and the trait distribution shifts toward the environmental optimum.
One fixed-seed regime over `fig11-evolution` (`meta_modelers_guide.composites.fig11-evolution`, seed=1) demonstrates the full arc over a 40-generation run. The founder `cell_0` sits at trait 0.0, far below the niche optimum (which starts at 1.0). Playing it forward: the lone founder divides -- `cell_0` is consumed and replaced by two daughters (`cell_1`, `cell_2`) on the first generation -- and the lineage grows by binary fission to carrying capacity (12 cells, reached at generation 14) and never exceeds it (death by selection caps it). Over the same run the selection optimum drifts monotonically from 1.0 to 1.80 (drift 0.02 per generation), and the population's mean trait -- starting at 0.0, a gap of 1.0 below the optimum -- climbs to ~1.68, closing the gap to ~0.12: the trait cloud tracks the drifting target. Because the composite is fixed-seed (seed=1), the whole trajectory (population sizes, mean trait, optimum, and the daughter-node ids) reproduces exactly run to run.
Every one of these is a genuine place-graph rewrite: the daughter nodes are fresh `tree[node]` vertices added at runtime with brand-new ids that are never reused, and the parents are deleted -- not values mutated in place. This is precisely the paper's §Evolution point (Fig 11): variation enters through discrete events (division + mutation) that edit the inventory of nodes, and selection -- an environmental niche optimum acting on the composition -- shifts the trait distribution toward the optimum over generations. It is a didactic, toy-real illustration of the Darwinian loop (variation + heritability + selection), not a calibrated population-genetics model.
claim: Composing one `population` (`tree[node]` of identically-schema'd `cell` nodes) with one `environment` niche through a single `PopulationEvolution` process reproduces the paper's §Evolution pattern (Fig 11) as a runnable place-graph rewrite: over a fixed-seed (seed=1) 40-generation run the founder cell (trait 0.0, a gap of 1.0 below the niche optimum) divides by binary fission -- the parent REPLACED by two mutated daughters -- grows to carrying capacity (12) and never exceeds it, while the selection optimum drifts monotonically from 1.0 to 1.80 and the population mean trait climbs from 0.0 to ~1.68, closing the trait-optimum gap from 1.0 to ~0.12. The distribution shifts toward the environmental optimum via variation (mutation) + heritability + selection, and division edits the place graph (parent id gone, two fresh daughter ids present) -- the whole trajectory is deterministic and reproduces exactly run to run. This is a didactic, toy-real illustration of the Darwinian loop, not a calibrated population-genetics model.

variants.name: fig11-mechanistic
variants.rationale: Real-mechanism upgrade (scientific-review revision, Oct 2026). The baseline fig11-evolution is a single-seed place-graph toy at carrying capacity 12, where — as the review notes — drift dominates and "the mean trait moving toward an imposed Gaussian optimum is expected by model design". This variant makes the population genetics quantitative and falsifiable: a real WRIGHT–FISHER step at a large carrying capacity (N=300), with viability selection, Gaussian mutation, explicit heritability and ancestry. The quantitative predictions the review asks for are theorems of the model and are tested over MANY independent seeds with intervals: selection tracks the moving optimum where NEUTRAL drift does not; realized heritability (parent–offspring regression) ≈ 1; the tracking lag obeys R=h²S and GROWS with the drift rate, running away beyond a critical rate (adaptation failure); and — optionally — fitness is DERIVED from an executable Michaelis–Menten metabolic tradeoff whose optimum a* drifts endogenously, rather than a prescribed Gaussian. The §Evolution (Fig 11) baseline is kept intact as the didactic place-graph smoke test.

key_assumptions: This `fig11-evolution` composite is **didactic / toy-real**: a small, illustrative minimal Darwinian loop built to look like Fig 11 and play forward -- NOT calibrated to any literature population-genetics target. The selection strength (Gaussian width sel_strength=0.6), mutation size (mut_sigma=0.28), per-generation division probability (div_rate=0.35), carrying capacity (12), optimum start (1.0) and drift (0.02/generation) are plausible hand-tuned magnitudes chosen to make variation -> selection -> adaptation legible within a 40-generation run, not fitted to a named organism, trait, or fitness landscape.

The trait is a single abstract heritable scalar and fitness is a single Gaussian kernel on trait<->optimum distance. There is no genotype, no genome, no recombination, no epistasis, no standing variation beyond what mutation injects at each division -- one locus, asexual binary fission.

Division is BINARY FISSION with parent replacement: a dividing cell is deleted and replaced by exactly two daughters, each trait = parent trait ± Gaussian(0, mut_sigma). The founder does not persist once it divides. This is a deliberate modeling choice (each division edits the place graph) rather than a budding/overlapping-generations scheme.

Population size is bounded by a hard carrying capacity (12): once the population overflows, the least-fit cells (furthest from the current optimum) are culled. Death is therefore purely selective and capacity-triggered -- there is no age, no random death, no resource depletion feedback (the niche `resource` field is carried but not consumed).

The composite is fixed-seed (seed=1), so the entire trajectory -- population sizes, mean trait, optimum, and the exact daughter-node ids -- is deterministic and reproduces exactly run to run. The pinned integers in the behavior tests are true regression pins under that seed, not run-to-run-variable magnitudes.
The rigorous, spatially-explicit cousin of this figure is `development-and-evolution` in the `draft-to-living-cell` investigation; this study does NOT restate that cousin's numbers as its own.
acceptance_criteria: The population grows from a single founder cell to carrying capacity (12) by binary fission and never exceeds capacity.
The environmental selection optimum drifts monotonically forward over the run (a moving target), reaching 1.80 from a start of 1.0.

The population mean trait -- starting far below the optimum (gap 1.0) -- moves toward the drifting optimum, closing the gap to well under its starting value, and the mean trait itself climbs (the cloud moves to the target, not the target to the cloud).

Division is a genuine place-graph rewrite by binary fission -- a dividing cell is REPLACED by exactly two fresh daughter nodes (parent id gone, two new ids present, net +1 cell), and cell ids are never reused.

units_and_time.time: 1 tick = 1 generation (dimensionless model time); the run is 40 such generations (41 emitted rows, t=0..40).
units_and_time.quantities: trait, selection_optimum, division_rate, sel_strength, mut_sigma, drift and capacity are dimensionless model quantities -- the trait is an abstract heritable scalar, the optimum a favored trait value, division_rate a per-generation probability; population size is a node count.
units_and_time.note: No quantity here is calibrated to a named organism, trait, or literature fitness landscape.

pass_if.provenance: prior: a single founder divides and the lineage grows until carrying capacity bounds it. Observed (seed=1): size 1 at t=0, rising to 12 by generation 14 and holding at 12 through t=40, with max size == 12 (never exceeds capacity). The ==12 pin is exact under the fixed seed; the grows-then-caps direction is the a-priori prediction (tests/test_fig11_dynamics.py::test_population_grows_to_capacity)

behavior_tests.description: Matched null (no-mutation): with mutation off, no new variation enters, so selection and drift erode the heritable variance toward zero and the population loses its capacity to respond. Isolates the role of mutation as the source of variation.

Predicted before running; verified by a drift sweep over many seeds.

measure.path: final lag vs optimum drift rate (20 seeds each)
measure.expr: lag monotone increasing in drift; runs away at high drift

pass_if.provenance: PROSPECTIVE_PREDICTION. Observed final lag rising 0.11 (drift 0.02) → 0.65 → 3.9 → 11.2 (drift 0.55) over 20-seed ensembles — monotone, with runaway at high drift (tests/test_fig11_mechanistic.py::test_adaptation_fails_when_optimum_moves_too_fast)

findings.statement: A `population` of identically-schema'd `cell` nodes coupled to an `environment` niche through one `PopulationEvolution` process reproduces the paper's §Evolution pattern (Fig 11b) as a runnable place-graph rewrite: under Gaussian selection for a drifting optimum, the population mean trait -- starting at 0.0, a gap of 1.0 below the niche optimum -- climbs to ~1.68 and closes the gap to ~0.12 as the optimum drifts from 1.0 to 1.80, the trait distribution shifting toward the environmental optimum via variation (mutation) + heritability + selection. Confirmed (seed=1, deterministic): optimum 1.0 -> 1.80 monotone, mean trait 0.0 -> ~1.68, gap 1.0 -> ~0.12.

Division is a genuine place-graph rewrite by binary fission (Fig 11a): a dividing cell is REPLACED by two fresh daughter nodes rather than duplicated in place. Confirmed (seed=1): the founder cell_0 is deleted and replaced by exactly two new nodes (cell_1, cell_2) at the first division; below carrying capacity every topology change adds exactly two daughters per vanished parent (appeared == 2*vanished); the lineage grows to capacity (12) and never exceeds it as death-by-selection culls the least-fit cells; and no retired cell id is ever reused -- each daughter is a genuinely new place-graph vertex.

evidence.observed: cell_0 -> {cell_1, cell_2} at first division; appeared == 2*vanished below capacity; size caps at 12; no id reused

findings.statement: The evolution run is fully deterministic under the pinned seed (seed=1): two independent builds of the composite emit byte-identical (size, mean_trait, optimum) trajectories and identical daughter-node ids. This makes the pinned integers in the behavior tests (final size 12, optimum 1.80) true regression pins rather than run-to-run-variable magnitudes.

evidence.observed: two independent runs produce identical trajectories and daughter ids

findings.statement: Reading the population tree's node contents at successive snapshots shows two structural features beyond the mean-trait track: standing variation and adaptation lag. (1) The final-generation snapshot is a trait CLOUD with width, not a converged point -- its 12 cell nodes span traits 1.47 to 1.91 (range 0.44, population standard deviation 0.131) around the optimum 1.80, because the Gaussian mutation injected at each binary fission keeps replenishing heritable variation that selection then shapes. (2) The population LAGS the moving target: the derived mean-trait gap to the drifting optimum closes below 0.4 only at generation 22 (from an initial gap of 1.0) and is still 0.12 at generation 40 -- the cloud chases but never catches the continuously drifting optimum, the signature of adaptation lag. Both are read from the per-generation population snapshots; confirmed in-memory (seed=1, deterministic).

evidence.observed: final snapshot (12 cells): traits min 1.470 / max 1.910 / range 0.440 / pop std 0.131 about optimum 1.80; derived mean-gap first < 0.4 at generation 22, gap 0.12 at generation 40

findings.statement: The §Evolution (Fig 11) adaptation claim is made QUANTITATIVE and distinguished from drift, over many seeds. In a real Wright–Fisher population (N=300), viability selection tracks the drifting optimum with a small bounded lag (0.39±0.04 over 40 seeds), while the matched NEUTRAL control (selection off) drifts away to a lag of 2.38±0.23 — a separation far larger than the across-seed spread. The realized heritability (parent–offspring regression) is 0.998, so the response obeys the breeder's equation R = h²·S, and a no-mutation control shows the variance eroding (0.21 → 0.001) when the source of variation is removed. This directly answers the review's point that the baseline's single-seed mean "tracking an imposed optimum" was expected by design: here the tracking is a statistical, controlled, heritability-grounded result.

evidence.observed: selection lag 0.39±0.04 vs neutral 2.38±0.23 (40 seeds); h²=0.998; no-mutation variance 0.21→0.001

findings.statement: A first-principles failure prediction is stated and passes: because the per-generation response is bounded (R = h²·S, limited by standing variance), the tracking lag must grow with the optimum's drift rate and run away once drift exceeds what selection can supply (an adaptation-failure / evolutionary-rescue threshold). A 20-seed drift sweep confirms the lag rising monotonically 0.11 → 11.2 as drift rises 0.02 → 0.55. Honest caveats, per the review: the mean trait moving toward the optimum is EXPECTED BY DESIGN — the content is the quantitative conditions (heritability, mutation supply, drift rate) under which adaptation succeeds or fails, the stochastic spread across seeds, and the explicit failure regime. At the baseline's small N=12 the across-seed drift is large; this variant uses N=300 and many replicates precisely to separate signal from drift.

evidence.observed: final lag 0.11 (drift 0.02) → 11.2 (drift 0.55), monotone runaway; single-seed = reproducibility only

findings.statement: Fitness can be DERIVED from an executable metabolic trait rather than prescribed. In the uptake mode each individual's trait is an uptake investment a; growth is a saturating Michaelis–Menten uptake of a drifting resource minus a quadratic cost, g(a) = Vmax·a·R/(Km+a) − cost·a², whose interior optimum a* drifts endogenously with the resource. The evolved mean trait climbs and tracks a* at correlation > 0.95 — the moving target is a consequence of a metabolic tradeoff, not an imposed Gaussian. Honest limits: still a single-locus asexual clonal model (no genome, recombination, epistasis), overdamped selection, and didactic rate constants; the quantitative lag in the uptake mode reflects a fast resource drift relative to the mutational supply.

evidence.observed: evolved mean tracks derived a* at corr > 0.95 over 50 generations (25 seeds)

regression_compatibility.basis: fig11-evolution.composite.json builds and runs to completion through the process-bigraph engine over a deterministic 40-generation run (tests/test_fig11_dynamics.py, 5 tests passing).

biological_validation.basis: Reported in two layers, per the review. BEHAVIORAL (baseline fig11-evolution): all four primary tests pass on a real 40-generation run — the population grows to capacity by binary fission and never exceeds it, the optimum drifts, the mean trait closes on it, and division replaces each parent with two fresh daughters. But this is a SINGLE seed at N=12, where drift dominates and mean-tracking is expected by design — behavioral verification / reproducibility, not robustness. MECHANISTIC (variant fig11-mechanistic): a real Wright–Fisher population (N=300) quantifies the claim over MANY seeds — selection tracks the optimum (lag 0.39±0.04) where the matched neutral control drifts away (2.38±0.23); realized heritability ≈ 1 so the response obeys R=h²S; a no-mutation control erodes the variance; adaptation fails predictably when drift outruns the response (lag 0.11→11.2 over a drift sweep); and fitness can be derived from an executable metabolic tradeoff. This is genuine, controlled, statistical mechanistic support. NOT yet empirical validation against a named organism's mutation rate, selection coefficient, or measured heritability — that is the stated next step.

explanatory_gain.basis: Realizing the paper's §Evolution pattern (Fig 11) as a runnable place-graph rewrite -- cell nodes ADDED and REMOVED at runtime as the trait distribution shifts toward an environmental optimum -- makes the paper's core §Evolution claim concrete: evolution changes not the state of one composition but the SPACE of compositions across generations. The trait cloud chasing a moving target, with parents genuinely replaced by mutated daughters on the place graph, is the Darwinian loop (variation + heritability + selection) made executable, not merely drawn.

conclusion:
## Claims
- Composing one `population` (`tree[node]` of identically-schema'd `cell` nodes) with one `environment` niche through a single `PopulationEvolution` process reproduces the paper's §Evolution pattern (Fig 11) as a runnable place-graph rewrite. Over a fixed-seed (seed=1) 40-generation run: the founder cell (trait 0.0, gap 1.0 below the optimum) divides by binary fission, grows to carrying capacity (12) and never exceeds it; the selection optimum drifts monotonically from 1.0 to 1.80; and the population mean trait climbs from 0.0 to ~1.68, closing the trait-optimum gap from 1.0 to ~0.12 -- the trait distribution shifting toward the environmental optimum via variation (mutation) + heritability + selection. The whole trajectory is deterministic and reproduces exactly run to run.
- Division (Fig 11a) is a genuine place-graph rewrite: a dividing cell is REPLACED by two fresh daughter nodes (parent id gone, two new ids present, net +1 cell), ids are never reused, and death by selection culls the least-fit cells at capacity -- nodes added and removed at runtime, editing the inventory of compositions rather than mutating values in place.
## Evidence
- **POPULATION-GROWS-TO-CAPACITY-BY-FISSION** -- size 1 (t=0) -> 12 by generation 14, held at 12 through t=40, max == 12 (never exceeds capacity)
- **SELECTION-OPTIMUM-DRIFTS** -- optimum 1.0 -> 1.80, monotone at drift 0.02/generation
- **MEAN-TRAIT-TRACKS-THE-DRIFTING-OPTIMUM** -- mean trait 0.0 (gap 1.0) -> ~1.68 (gap ~0.12); the mean climbs by > 1.0
- **DIVISION-IS-BINARY-FISSION-PLACE-GRAPH-REWRITE** -- cell_0 -> {cell_1, cell_2} at first division; appeared == 2*vanished below capacity; no id reused
- **TRAJECTORY-IS-DETERMINISTIC** -- two independent builds emit identical trajectories and daughter ids (seed=1)
## Limitations
- This composite is didactic / toy-real: a minimal Darwinian loop (one abstract heritable scalar trait, one Gaussian fitness kernel) with hand-tuned magnitudes, not calibrated to any organism, trait, or literature fitness landscape.
- No genome, recombination, epistasis, or standing variation beyond mutation; asexual binary fission at one locus. Death is purely selective and capacity-triggered (no age, random death, or resource-depletion feedback -- the niche `resource` field is carried but not consumed).
- The rigorous cousin of this figure is `development-and-evolution` in the `draft-to-living-cell` investigation; its numbers are NOT restated here.
## Next steps
- Sweep selection strength, mutation size, and drift rate to show the adaptation-lag trade-off (a faster drift or weaker selection leaves a larger residual gap).
- Add standing genetic variation / recombination to move from a single-locus toy toward a population-genetics-flavored model.

if_primary_tests_pass.biological_validation: The §Evolution pattern (Fig 11) is demonstrated at the toy-real (uncalibrated) level, with genuine runtime place-graph rewrites (cell nodes added and removed) and a trait distribution shifting toward a drifting environmental optimum, rather than a scripted trajectory.

diagnose: the population fails to grow to capacity (div_rate or fitness too low relative to the run length, or the founder's trait sits so far from the optimum that fitness ~ 0)
the optimum fails to drift (the drift parameter is zero or the environment output is not being written back)
the mean trait fails to close on the optimum (selection too weak, mutation too large/small, or the population is too small to hold favorable variants against drift)
division does not replace the parent with two daughters (the fission rewrite is broken, or ids are being reused rather than freshly minted)
if_primary_tests_fail.block_downstream: any future study reusing the PopulationEvolution place-graph-rewrite pattern (e.g. a multi-trait or multi-niche extension)

limitations: This `fig11-evolution` composite is didactic / toy-real -- a minimal Darwinian loop built to look like Fig 11 and play forward, NOT calibrated to any literature population-genetics target. The selection strength (0.6), mutation size (0.28), division probability (0.35), carrying capacity (12), optimum start (1.0) and drift (0.02/generation) are plausible hand-tuned magnitudes chosen to make variation -> selection -> adaptation legible within a 40-generation run, not fitted to a named organism, trait, or fitness landscape.

The trait is a single abstract heritable scalar and fitness a single Gaussian kernel on trait<->optimum distance -- no genotype, genome, recombination, epistasis, or standing variation beyond what mutation injects at each division. One locus, asexual binary fission.

Division is binary fission with parent replacement (a dividing cell is deleted and replaced by two mutated daughters); the founder does not persist once it divides. This is a deliberate modeling choice (each division edits the place graph), not a budding/overlapping-generations scheme.

Population size is bounded by a hard carrying capacity (12) with purely selective, capacity-triggered death -- no age, no random death, no resource-depletion feedback (the niche `resource` field is carried but not consumed).

The composite is fixed-seed (seed=1), so the entire trajectory -- sizes, mean trait, optimum, and daughter-node ids -- is deterministic and reproduces exactly; the pinned integers are true regression pins under that seed.
The rigorous cousin of this figure is `development-and-evolution` in the `draft-to-living-cell` investigation; this study does NOT restate that cousin's numbers as its own.

Mechanistic variant (fig11-mechanistic) — scope and honest limits: it adds the quantitative, many-seed population genetics the baseline lacked (real Wright–Fisher at N=300, neutral and no-mutation controls, realized heritability, a drift-rate adaptation-failure sweep, and an optional executable-trait fitness), directly addressing the single-seed/N=12/expected-by-design critique. But it is a SINGLE-LOCUS, ASEXUAL, CLONAL model: one abstract heritable scalar, no genome/recombination/epistasis/linkage, viability selection only (no explicit demography beyond fixed N), and all rate constants (mutation σ, selection strength, drift, cost) are didactic — NOT fitted to a named organism's mutation rate, selection coefficient, or measured heritability. The mean trait tracking the optimum is expected by model design; the evidence is the controlled, many-seed quantification of WHEN and HOW WELL it does so, not that it does so at all. Empirical calibration remains the stated next step.
falsifiability: Overturned if the population fails to grow to carrying capacity by binary fission or exceeds it, if the selection optimum fails to drift monotonically, if the mean trait fails to close on the drifting optimum (the gap not shrinking, or the mean not climbing), if division fails to replace a parent with exactly two fresh daughter nodes, if cell ids are reused, or if the fixed-seed trajectory fails to reproduce exactly across independent builds.

Mechanistic (the decisive figure): a real Wright–Fisher population with heritable variation, mutation and ancestry, quantified over MANY seeds. What to look for: (A) the trait density over generations (N=600) with the moving optimum overlaid — the cloud tracks the drifting target with a lag. (B) a lineage genealogy coloured by trait — a real phylogeny, not a scripted path. (C) replicate means over 40 seeds with 90% intervals (the steady lag is the R=h²S selection balance). (D) selection vs the matched NEUTRAL control — selection holds a small lag while neutral drift wanders away, so the tracking is really selection, not drift. experiment: Run the `fig11-evolution` composite (`PopulationEvolution` over a population tree[node] of identically-schema'd cell nodes + an environment niche whose selection optimum drifts) to completion over 40 generations through the process-bigraph engine, and measure whether variation (heritable mutation at binary fission) + selection (a Gaussian fitness kernel on trait<->optimum distance, with death-by-selection at carrying capacity) is enough to shift the population's trait distribution toward a drifting environmental optimum, while division genuinely edits the place graph (parent replaced by two daughters).
result: Over a fixed-seed (seed=1) 40-generation run, the founder cell (trait 0.0, a gap of 1.0 below the niche optimum) divides by binary fission -- cell_0 replaced by two daughters cell_1, cell_2 -- and the lineage grows to carrying capacity (12 by generation 14) and never exceeds it. The selection optimum drifts monotonically from 1.0 to 1.80 (drift 0.02/generation) and the population mean trait climbs from 0.0 to ~1.68, closing the trait-optimum gap from 1.0 to ~0.12: the trait distribution shifts toward the environmental optimum via variation + heritability + selection. Division is a genuine place-graph rewrite throughout -- below capacity every topology change adds exactly two fresh daughters per vanished parent, ids are never reused, and death-by-selection culls the least-fit cells at capacity. The whole trajectory (sizes, mean trait, optimum, daughter ids) is deterministic and reproduces exactly across independent builds. The paper's §Evolution pattern (Fig 11) holds as a runnable place-graph rewrite at the toy-real (uncalibrated) level: evolution changes the space of compositions across generations, not the state of a single composition. The rigorous cousin is `development-and-evolution` in the `draft-to-living-cell` investigation.

biological_validation.basis: Reported in two layers, per the review. BEHAVIORAL (baseline fig11-evolution): all four primary tests pass on a real 40-generation run — the population grows to capacity by binary fission and never exceeds it, the optimum drifts, the mean trait closes on it, and division replaces each parent with two fresh daughters. But this is a SINGLE seed at N=12, where drift dominates and mean-tracking is expected by design — behavioral verification / reproducibility, not robustness. MECHANISTIC (variant fig11-mechanistic): a real Wright–Fisher population (N=300) quantifies the claim over MANY seeds — selection tracks the optimum (lag 0.39±0.04) where the matched neutral control drifts away (2.38±0.23); realized heritability ≈ 1 so the response obeys R=h²S; a no-mutation control erodes the variance; adaptation fails predictably when drift outruns the response (lag 0.11→11.2 over a drift sweep); and fitness can be derived from an executable metabolic tradeoff. This is genuine, controlled, statistical mechanistic support. NOT yet empirical validation against a named organism's mutation rate, selection coefficient, or measured heritability — that is the stated next step.

regression_compatibility.basis: fig11-evolution.composite.json builds and runs to completion through the process-bigraph engine over a deterministic 40-generation run (tests/test_fig11_dynamics.py, 5 tests passing).

explanatory_gain.basis: Realizing the paper's §Evolution pattern (Fig 11) as a runnable place-graph rewrite -- cell nodes ADDED and REMOVED at runtime as the trait distribution shifts toward an environmental optimum -- makes the paper's core §Evolution claim concrete: evolution changes not the state of one composition but the SPACE of compositions across generations. The trait cloud chasing a moving target, with parents genuinely replaced by mutated daughters on the place graph, is the Darwinian loop (variation + heritability + selection) made executable, not merely drawn.

derived.insight: A `population` of identically-schema'd `cell` nodes coupled to an `environment` niche through one `PopulationEvolution` process reproduces the paper's §Evolution pattern (Fig 11b) as a runnable place-graph rewrite: under Gaussian selection for a drifting optimum, the population mean trait -- starting at 0.0, a gap of 1.0 below the niche optimum -- climbs to ~1.68 and closes the gap to ~0.12 as the optimum drifts from 1.0 to 1.80, the trait distribution shifting toward the environmental optimum via variation (mutation) + heritability + selection. Confirmed (seed=1, deterministic): optimum 1.0 -> 1.80 monotone, mean trait 0.0 -> ~1.68, gap 1.0 -> ~0.12.
